name: Line-Following Robot
shortDescription: An Arduino-based line-following robot built for Track Trace 2.0, where the team earned third place in 2026.
overview: This project involved building and testing a line-following robot for Track Trace 2.0. The robot used an Arduino Nano, infrared sensors, a motor driver, and a PCB-based electronics setup to detect and follow a track. The team achieved third place.
objectives: Build a robot capable of following a marked track.
Integrate the controller, sensors, motor driver, and electronics.
Test the robot and identify issues before and during competition rounds.
role: Tested robot behavior on the track.
Checked code for errors and helped troubleshoot problems.
Contributed to the robot's design and assembly.
features: Testing across practice and competition tracks
challenges: Robot performance had to be checked repeatedly against different track conditions and turns.
Hardware, wiring, and code needed to work together, making testing and error checking important.
learnings: How sensors, a microcontroller, and a motor driver work together in a mobile robot.
The value of repeated testing and systematic troubleshooting.
How mechanical assembly and electronics reliability affect performance.
results: Third place in Track Trace 2.0 in 2026. The user's contribution focused on testing, code error checking, design, and assembly; the user was not the team leader.
